findings.title: Crash when Google Meet has no destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then dereferenced with `.integration`. For a Google Meet event with no destination calendar (null or empty array), it is undefined, so booking creation throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining/defaulting here.

findings.title: Video meeting references lose credentialId
findings.body: For non-calendar results (the dedicated video meeting), `credentialId` is now hard-coded to `undefined`. The previous code used `result.credentialId`, which is how the video credential was persisted on the booking reference. Since `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, this regression leaves video meetings behind on cancellation and breaks later video updates.

findings.title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when no main destination exists
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so other collective hosts' destination calendars are never added and those hosts do not get calendar events. Initializing to `[]` has to be done carefully so the organizer's fallback-calendar path is still preserved.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns an EventResult without either field. Before this change the code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. Now location changes persist new booking references with both values undefined, so later updates/cancellations cannot locate the actual calendar and credential.

findings.title: Stale credential reused when a reference's credential is missing
findings.body: `credential` is declared outside the reference loop. If a reference has a credentialId that is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup fails or yields no app slug, the variable still holds the previous reference's credential and is passed to `updateEvent` with the current reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This can update/delete the wrong host's calendar. Reset `credential` per iteration and skip/report when it cannot be resolved.

findings.title: Legacy destination without credentialId loses externalCalendarId on references
findings.body: When a destination calendar has no credentialId, this branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the destination's externalId. `EventManager.create` now builds `referencesToCreate[].externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId`, so it is undefined even though the destination identifies a specific calendar. Previously the reference used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so this can make later update/delete target the primary or wrong calendar. Pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

findings.title: Office365 create ignores credentialId and always uses the first destination
findings.body: `createEvent` always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. EventManager invokes it once per destination credential; for a second collective host, the first host's calendar id is used with the second host's token, usually causing a 404 or writing to the wrong calendar. The same first-only pattern exists in larkcalendar and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts. CalDAV is especially dangerous: filtering the second host's calendars against the first host's externalId can produce an empty list and return success without creating anything.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to the same falsy value
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which only matches a destination whose externalId is null/undefined. For legacy references without an externalCalendarId this leaves `calendarId` undefined in `updateEvent` (the update fails) and falls back to primary in `deleteEvent` (line 317), deleting from the wrong calendar. Use a real fallback destination or require the external id.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation still only deletes the organizer's calendar events
findings.body: The new outer loop over all calendar references enters the recurring branch, but inside it ignores the current `calendarCredential`/`calendar` and iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's credentials only). It also uses `.find` to pick only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. For a recurring collective booking, other hosts' calendar events are never deleted, and the same deletion work is repeated once per current reference. Use the current reference's credential and iterate all references.

findings.title: Collective confirmation flow does not load all hosts' destination calendars
findings.body: This handler creates calendar events for bookings that required confirmation. It builds `destinationCalendar` from the single booking destination or the confirming user only, and `handleNewBooking` persists only the first destination on the booking. Other collective hosts' destination calendars are never loaded, so confirming a collective booking still creates events for only one host. The same gap exists in the payment webhooks (`features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts` and `paypal-webhook.ts`), which also create calendar events after payment.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED changes organization slug creation
findings.body: This unrelated change flips the condition: previously `slug` was set when team billing was disabled and `requestedSlug` when enabled; now `slug` is set when billing is enabled, and neither field is set when billing is disabled. That changes organization URL/slug behavior for self-hosted/billing-disabled deployments and is unrelated to the calendar fix. If not intentional, revert it.
